crystal: ordinary hexagonal ice (ice Ih), the phase of IAPWS R10-06(2009)
source: WP4 of batch 2026-09-24-coolprop-low-temperature (RANGE_EXTRAPOLATION_PLAN.md section 6, decision 4 A): heat-capacity segments fitted to the Gibbs function of ice Ih, IAPWS R10-06(2009), Revised Release on an Equation of State 2006 for H2O Ice Ih (Feistel and Wagner 2006, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 35, 1021), free release https://iapws.org; anchored to the network's liquid water (IAPWS-IF97 Region 1) at the triple point. Its sublimation pressure is IAPWS R14-08(2011) equation 6, in the water record. Fit and check script: tools/unified-thermo-port-ice/fit (R10-06's seven check values reproduced to 2.2e-12 before fitting). Non-commercial project; IAPWS releases cited for provenance.

segments.source: least squares on relative c_p of R10-06 at 611.657 Pa, every 0.25 K from 10 to 60 K, constrained to meet the upper segment at 60 K (9.557081 J/(mol K) on both sides); worst c_p deviation 4.5e-3 (at 10 K)
least squares on relative c_p of R10-06 at 611.657 Pa, every 0.25 K from 60 to 273.16 K; 37.77 J/(mol K) at the triple point, 15.74 at 100 K; worst c_p deviation 3.9e-3

molar_volume.source: linear form at the triple point as approved for WP4: 19.65 cm3/mol (916.7 kg/m3, R10-06 916.709), expansion 1.6e-4 /K (R10-06 1.599e-4 at the triple point), compressibility 1.2e-10 /Pa (R10-06 1.178e-10); against R10-06 -0.01 % at 263.15 K, -0.90 % at 111.6 K, -2.4 % at 10 K. R10-06's validity: up to 210 MPa.

anchor.source: the triple point of water, 273.16 K and 611.657 Pa (IAPWS R10-06 and R14-08); fusion enthalpy 6007 J/mol at the triple point (R10-06 with IAPWS-95: 333.43 kJ/kg). The melting line follows from the record by Clapeyron with the network's liquid at the anchor (decision 5 A): about -7.42e-8 K/Pa, 272.42 K at 10 MPa.

coverage.evidence: WP4 fit against IAPWS R10-06 at 611.657 Pa over 10 to 273.16 K: c_p within 4.5e-3, h - h(273.16 K) within 1.7e-4 (0.34 J/mol), s - s(273.16 K) within 1.7e-4; molar volume within 0.9 % above 111.6 K (2.4 % at 10 K). Pressure enters through the linear volume only.
